newsitem.title: CHINA: China state firm profits slid 75.8 pct in Jan-Sept.
newsitem.headline: China state firm profits slid 75.8 pct in Jan-Sept.

text.p: China's state industry earned net profits of 11.28 billion yuan ($1.36 billion) in the January-September period, down 75.8 percent from a year ago, an official from the State Statistical Bureau said on Thursday.
The unprofitable portion of state industry had a combined deficit of 65.12 billion yuan in the nine-month period, up 45.7 percent from a year ago, he said.
Of the total 68,800 state-owned industrial enterprises in China, 31,400 lost money in the first nine months of 1996, up 17.6 percent from a year ago, he said.
More than 200 state firms have been declared bankrupt to date, he said without giving further details.
China has prepared 20 billion yuan in capital reserves to write off the bad debts of bankrupt state firms this year, the official People's Daily said today.
China has been tring to reform its state-run enterprises, which are often overstaffed and unable to compete effectively in the domestic or overseas markets. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
